record.what_it_does: Neo4j is a graph database platform (self-managed or the Aura cloud service) queried via Cypher, with a separate management API for provisioning and administering cloud database instances.
record.auth_notes: The Aura control-plane API (create/manage database instances, tenants, snapshots) uses OAuth2 client-credentials: exchange a Client ID/Secret for a 1-hour Bearer access token at https://api.neo4j.io/oauth/token. The actual database Query API / HTTP API (running Cypher against a specific instance) instead authorizes each request with a Basic or Bearer Authorization header tied to that database's own user credentials or SSO token — there is no delegated end-user OAuth login flow for querying data.
record.access_notes: AuraDB Free tier can be created with no credit card, and 'All tiers can create Aura API credentials' immediately from the console — a developer gets working OAuth2 client credentials and a running database instantly.
record.main_blocker: no unified delegated-auth flow for querying arbitrary users' databases — the agent needs each user's own instance URI plus Basic/Bearer DB credentials, separate from the OAuth2 flow that only manages Aura infrastructure

evidence.quote: The Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication.
Both basic and bearer authentication are supported.
All tiers can create Aura API credentials.
Neo4j MCP implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard that lets applications connect to external data sources and tools.

record.open_questions: Whether the Aura API's OAuth2 client-credentials model (one client per account, no third-party authorization/redirect flow) is compatible with a true multi-tenant agent toolkit, or whether it only suits single-tenant/internal automation; also unclear how a toolkit would obtain per-end-user database connection credentials at scale.
